headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between marketingskills and opik.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a reads and writes filesystem content and its skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” so attacker-controlled content can flow into agent_a outputs. agent_b exposes a REST API and broad egress, so if it consumes agent_a outputs as inputs, prompt-like content can propagate. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-generated text as instructions or prompts, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance tags, attacker content can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Prefix all agent_a outputs with immutable provenance labels.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files or API payloads.
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filtering at the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read and write files and touches marketing content and product marketing context; agent_b has broad network egress and REST API access. If they share a workspace, agent_a’s files can be exposed through agent_b’s outbound requests or logs. No secret-handling or residency controls are documented, so the safe assumption is a default shared-data leakage path exists.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or mounted workspace, file contents can traverse to agent_b.
IF agent_b forwards request bodies or context to external services, marketing content may leak.
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions.
Remove sensitive marketing drafts before handoff.
Turn off outbound API calls for shared runs.
Review outbound payloads for file content.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on agent_b egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances; agent_b has broad network egress and REST API calls. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared state, concurrent writes and API-driven updates can race and corrupt artifacts. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the dangerous default is unresolved contention.
conditions: IF both agents write the same directory or git state, conflicts can corrupt outputs.
IF agent_b updates shared resources while agent_a runs subprocesses, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize runs with a simple operator checklist.
Freeze shared files before agent_b starts.
Avoid concurrent instances of agent_a on the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a’s marketing outputs can become inputs to agent_b’s REST/API workflows, and agent_a’s sandboxing explicitly says skills “reference each other and build on shared context.” If agent_b treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. There is no documented verification gate between them, but direct action authority is not proven.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output without independent verification, mistakes propagate.
IF agent_b renders or acts on agent_a-generated claims, downstream errors multiply.
mitigations: Require a human review before agent_b consumes agent_a output.
Add a verification checklist for factual claims.
Keep source citations attached to agent_a outputs.
Limit agent_b to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/traceability checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches marketing content and product marketing context, while agent_b documents no sensitive data classes or special compliance obligations. The pair does not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, but agent_b’s broad egress means any future regulated content would need review. Because only agent_a has a documented data class, the other agent is not cited for a specific compliance mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into agent_a’s workspace, compliance review is required.
IF agent_b is used to transmit regulated content across borders, residency controls become relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Label marketing drafts by sensitivity.
Review outbound destinations before runs.
Document retention expectations for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
